what-do-historians-actually-do.title: What Do Historians Actually Do?
what-do-historians-actually-do.essential: How can we use historical evidence to investigate what do historians actually do?
paragraphs: Historians construct explanations from incomplete traces of the past. Primary sources, secondary arguments and archival silences demand separate kinds of scrutiny. This lesson focuses on what do historians actually do? within historical research and historiography. Begin by establishing the relevant time, place, actors, and the terms used in the inquiry. Ask which parts of the historical account are supported by contemporaneous evidence and which are later interpretations.

Historians distinguish a record made at the time from a later interpretation, but a primary document is not automatically accurate. A government census, a diary, and a newspaper can each reveal different aspects of the same event. Missing voices, translation choices, collection practices, and surviving archives shape the possible answers. A good historical argument states exactly what its evidence can and cannot establish.
